uncited: All methods in this family share the goal of approximating the integral of the radiative transfer equation for multiple scattering orders without solving it iteratively per frame.
Real-time approximations for volumetric rendering emerged as hardware capabilities improved, allowing for more complex lighting calculations within frame budgets.
Early approaches relied on precomputed lighting (baking) [2169-precomputed-lighting-baking.md].

The introduction of voxel-based techniques like Voxel Cone Tracing [1454-voxel-cone-tracing.md] and Froxel-based methods [1919-froxel-based-volumetric-rendering.md] enabled dynamic global illumination in participating media.

More recent methods, such as Modular Transfer [1249-modular-transfer.md] and Light Volume Lookup [1188-multiple-scattering-approximation-via-light-volume-lookup.md], focus on specific types of media (e.g., structured fabrics, smoke) and use advanced precomputation and approximation strategies to handle multiple scattering efficiently.
The field continues to evolve with the integration of hardware ray tracing [3648-hardware-ray-tracing-global-illumination.md] and machine learning techniques.
